answer: A sybil defense can work like a lantern in fog: every agent must lock a refundable stake before its signal is accepted, so one identity costs real capital and a thousand fakes cost a thousand stakes. A burst of fresh accounts rises like a plume of smoke, visible against the public registry of past work, and peers refuse signals from identities with no history. If an agent cheats, anyone can challenge and slash its stake, so attacking costs the stake plus the lost reputation, while honest agents keep their deposit and earn fees over time.
